# Blackwater Lake · Book II, pp. 48–57
# Generated by the extractor — fix the extractor, not this file.
PAGE	48
P	In the west of the <b>Steplands</b> (page 372), in the shadow of the <b>Huffel Peaks</b> (page 236), there is a large and placid lake. A low ridge surrounds it, and a wide, rocky shore. The Aberzh River flows in from the west. No rivers or streams flow out.
P	The water is dark, and very deep, and very, very still. It is always cold but never freezes.
P	There are no waves. The wind shuns the surface. No birds dare alight.
P	This was once great Dulenn, city of Dark
P	Waters, the slow-beating heart of the <b>Stone Lords</b>' vast domain (page 382).
P	Whereas <b>Teirstered</b> (page 438) was a city of towers and splendor, Dulenn was a solemn place. A quiet warren, carved and sung from bedrock with the beauty of a limestone cave.
P	There was no lake, then. Not above the ground. But it was called "Dark Waters" for a reason. For seven deep tunnels led to seven mighty seals, each guarded by Stone Lord sentinels who sang a ceaseless lulling song. Behind those doors was a vast and lightless lake. A hole in the earth. A <b>Mouth of Daagon</b> (page 55).
P	When the <b>Green Lords</b> (page 210) roused the Things Below to help them quell the <b>Fae</b> (page 94), the seals below Dulenn cracked. Daagon began to whisper.
P	Began to sing. Resentment grew among the Stone Lords' human servants. Leaders rose among them: cunning, confident, and eloquent, knowing things they oughtn't, awash in uncanny power. Cults of liberation formed. A conspiracy grew.
PAGE	49
P	Seven sorcerers infiltrated Dulenn. They found the tunnels. They slew the sentinels.
P	They broke the seals.
P	And Daagon, Who Waits in Deep Water, waited no more. It thrashed. It opened its yawning dark wet jaws. Dulenn fell into the earth. And the Dark Water, the Blackwater, surged in to flood the hole.
H2	Impressions
HR
B	Striations in nearby outcrops, tilted towards the lake
B	The damp, mineral smell of wet stone
B	Clouds, stars, shoreline—all reflected in the lake
B	Stillness, quiet, echoes of the slightest sound
B	At times: thick banks of fog, wet, cloying, isolating Tip: lower your voice; speak slowly, softly, make them lean in to hear you.
H2	Hooks
HR
B	<b>Servants of Daagon</b> (page 56) are roaming further from the lake than usual.
B	A <b>thrall</b> (page 435) of Daagon drags a victim here to sacrifice.
B	A <b>deathless one</b>'s (page 46) tether is hidden near the lake.
B	Hillfolk <b>spirit-talkers</b> (page 235) sing a certain song here every 7 years to keep the lake subdued.
B	A dangerous artifact needs to be cast into the Mouth of Daagon.
B	Certain NPCs hear a silent song, calling them to Blackwater Lake.
H2	Getting there
HR
P	To reach Blackwater Lake from Stonetop:
C	First you must travel to the Steplands, which will take at least 4 days.
C	From there, it will take at least 2 days and corresponding amount of supplies
C	You need a knowledgeable guide.
C	Even then, you risk getting lost near the lake.
C	The terrain itself is treacherous, you risk injury on the way.
C	The way is grueling, you risk exhausting yourselves/your resources.
C	You need to watch out for horrors from the lake.
C	The way is perilous, plagued with danger.
PAGE	50
H2	Areas
HR
B	<b>Nearby hills:</b> A soft place, where paths might change in the fog, full of ruins, <b>barrow mounds</b> (page 39), and <b>caves</b> (page 380). Bedrock and ruins all tilt towards the lake.
B	<b>Outer ridge:</b> An escarpment that rings the lake, dropping 50-100' to the shores. Lightly wooded up top. Holds a number of ruins, buried at odd angles, some poking out.
B	<b>Shore:</b> Extends 100-200' from the outer ridge. Lots of rubble, much of it ancient masonry. Thick lichen, grass that leans away from the lake.
B	<b>The Aberzh River:</b> Cuts through the western ridge, then widens and flows lazily to the lake. Muddy, shallow, rocky. Lots of dark algae.
B	<b>The Pillar:</b> On the north shore, 40' wide and over 100' tall. Made of salvaged masonry stones, crudely stacked. No obvious entrance. A precarious climb. Feels cursed.
B	<b>The lake:</b> About 2 x 3 miles. Impossibly still, dark, reflective. Always cold, never freezes. Hundreds of feet deep near the center.

PAGE	51
P	1d12 ruin or barrow
HR
P	1 Partly collapsed mound of earth and stones, each carved with fearrunes. Holds bones, clay vessels full of rotted grain.
P	2 Warehouse-sized bunker of massive blocks, buried at a severe angle. Bay doors visible, heavily marred, but still intact.
P	3 Warren of human-sized rooms, dug into outer ridge. Confusing layout, odd angles, unstable, lit by glowing crystals.
P	4 Door into the ridge, leading to a crude, vaulted room. Holds a 12' statue of a squat, fishy beast. Its mouth opens to a deep shaft.
P	5 Dozens of makerglass tubes, each smaller than the last, lined up in ranks and fused together. Chime hauntingly when struck.
P	6 Walls of a cubical stone room with many niches. Tilted ~30°. Crystalline fixture in one wall. Words spoken here blare from somewhere across the lake.
P	7 Series of dissimilar rooms and tunnels, leading to a massive underground amphitheater, like a cyst in the earth. Largely flooded.
P	1d12 ruin or barrow
P	8 Stone head, bigger than a house, barely recognizable. Eye sockets open to a chamber. Interior walls covered in runes, useless levers.
P	9 Barrow on the ridge, hidden by trees, brush. An open doorway.
P	Inside: a withered corpse bound by bronze, a pile of offerings.
P	10 Small hill of stacked stones; one slab hides a door. Inside, an icy crystal lures in wraiths, binds them; scores are trapped already.
P	11 Cavernous, buried room, tilted but mostly whole. Full of chisels and <b>warded pavestones</b> (page 271):
P	mostly smashed, a few in progress, some buried but intact.
P	12 Onion-shaped dome of stone, ~30' across. Hollow, an opening facing down, water pooling impossibly on the ceiling inside.
P	The above are just examples. To create more Stone Lord ruins, see page 386 but roll for condition with disadvantage.
P	Those that are at all intact will be tilted and askew, and are likely to have been <b>reclaimed</b> (page 36) by the Barrow Builders at some point.
P	To create more barrows, see page 39.

H3	Fog
P	Fog forms often, especially on breezy, warm days or during still, chilly nights. Sometimes it comes with no warning. And sometimes, reality becomes…
P	malleable… in the fog.
P	• Have mist start to gather, thicken

H3	The Blackwater
P	The lake is always frigid but never freezes over. It is weirdly dark and still, smooth like glass. Any disturbance ripples out and out and out. It feels like it is sleeping. Like it's lying in wait.
P	Hazards include:
B	Instinctive dread, from a generational fear of water
B	The fact that they probably can't swim
B	Shivering cold, the threat of debilities or even <b>hypothermia</b> (page 489)
B	Poor footing (slick rocks, mud, algae)
B	Steep, unexpected drop-offs
B	Getting dragged down by their gear

H3	Drowning
P	When you <b><i>plunge beneath the water</i></b>, hold Breath equal to 1 + your CON. If you first took a deep breath, hold 2 extra
P	Breath.
P	When you <b><i>make a move while under the</i></b> <b><i>Blackwater</i></b>, and that move involves a roll, choose 1 of the following after the move is resolved:
B	Spend 1 Breath
B	Mark a debility
B	Lose yourself in the Blackwater When you <b><i>lose yourself in the Blackwater</i></b>, time seems to stop and you find yourself adrift in a watery, hungry void. Roll +WIS:
P	<b>on a 7+</b>, you snap back to reality, somehow holding 2 Breath. But also, <b>on a 10+</b>, choose 1; on a 7-9, choose 2:
B	Gain a mark (page 432) of Daagon; you are now <i>corrupted</i>
B	Name something you possess that you love or treasure; it's gone
B	Choose something about yourself that you value (a move, your instinct, something about your appearance); lose it
P	<b>On a 6-</b>, either embrace Daagon as your master (gain the Thrall insert), or else make one last move before you are swallowed by the <b>Mouth of Daagon</b> (next page).
ICON	icons/danger.svg
H3	Call of Daagon
P	<b>Daagon</b> (page 419) still sings its silent song. It calls out to the weak-willed, and to those who nurse jealousy or greed in their souls. It whispers to them from afar, and compels them towards Blackwater Lake. It urges the weak-willed to enter the water and be devoured. To the jealous and the greedy, it offers power, wealth, or immortality. For a price, of course.
PAGE	55
HR
ICON	icons/danger.svg
H3	Mouth of Daagon
P	At the bottom of the lake, hundreds of feet down, is a Mouth of Daagon.
P	Anything dropped into the deep water will make its way there in time. Valuables left on the shore or cast into the shallows will likely be found by the <b>servants</b> (page 56) and delivered to the Mouth on your behalf. Dangerous artifacts left for the servants might be delivered and consumed, or not.
P	When <b><i>the Mouth swallows something</i></b>, Daagon consumes it utterly. When <b><i>the</i></b> <b><i>Mouth swallows someone</i></b>, they are gone, body and soul.
P	When you <b><i>feed the Mouth with something</i></b> <b><i>or someone beloved</i></b> (by anyone, not just you), Daagon rewards you.
P	1d6 reward
HR
P	1 A physical change (scales, rubbery flesh, gills, a tentacle, etc.) and perhaps a gift (page 432) to go with it
P	2 An item of luxury or status (Value 2)
P	3 A precious item (Value 3)
P	4 A "priceless" item (Value 4)
P	5 A way to best your rivals or defeat your enemies
P	6 A way to acquire great power or long life Whatever the reward, it arrives soon: while you sleep, in your dreams, or via vision or coincidence or happy accident.

H3	Servants of Daagon
P	<i>Terrifying</i>, <i>violent</i>, <i>wretched</i>, either <i>corrupted</i> or <i>emanation</i>, see below
P	<b>HP</b> variable; <b>Armor</b> variable

P	<b>Instinct</b> to devour, then to steal
P	• Emerge from deep water or thick fog
P	• Snatch up something valued/treasured
P	• See below
P	Horrid things, wet and wriggling. Maybe they're <b>emanations</b> (page 436) of Daagon, or mortal beings so thoroughly corrupted as to seem utterly alien to this world. They crawl forth. They feast on flesh and bone. They drag home wealth and beauty and treasured things to feed their master's hunger.
P	Choose or roll for their number appearing and their size. Then pick or roll for 1d4 traits and 1d4 additional moves. Think about things that live in the water. Imagine the creatures implied by the results.
